resources.string: Personal, open-source paperless document app. Files are the source of truth.
Once per start, ask GitHub whether a newer version has been released.
Moves PDFs after import and metadata changes; files are never overwritten.

PDFs saved to this folder (for example by a scanner app) are imported into the library automatically, and their text is recognized.
When on, source files are deleted from the watched folder once they are safely in the library. When off, they stay and are simply skipped as duplicates on later scans.
Uses an AI provider of your choice to suggest tags and answer questions about your documents.
Requests go directly to this provider with your own API key. Pick Custom for any other OpenAI-compatible server.
OpenAI-compatible server, e.g. %1$s or %2$s. A pasted %3$s URL also works.

Load the provider's models with the arrow, or type a model ID.
How much the model may think before answering. Default keeps the server's behaviour; not every provider or model supports every level.
Requests send document text to the configured server.
Default max suggested tags per document
Default number of tags the assistant proposes per document (%1$d-%2$d); can be changed per run in Bulk edit.
Default max new tags per document
Default number of brand-new tags (not already in your library) the assistant may propose per document (%1$d-%2$d; 0 = never); can be changed per run in Bulk edit.

Right after a document is scanned or imported and its text is read, the assistant applies tags from your existing tags (it never creates new ones) and fills in every field marked "Let AI fill this in" when it is still empty. Applied without review, so each new document costs one request.
Read text with the assistant instead of on-device text recognition

Uses the model to read every scanned page, which handles handwriting, tables and faint scans far better than on-device text recognition. This costs one request per page, not per document, and it also re-reads documents that on-device text recognition already handled. Documents longer than %1$d pages keep using on-device text recognition here; you can still ask for those one at a time. Leave this off to read text on-device and use "Read text with assistant" on individual documents instead.

Checks three things in turn: that the server answers, that the model replies to a question, and that it can read text off a page image. Costs two very small requests. Checking stops at the first failure, since everything after it would fail for the same reason.
"%1$s" has been switched off: this model cannot read page images, so it would spend a request per page and return nothing.

Keeps this library in a folder of your own cloud storage: PDFs, details and trash travel as plain files, so every device connected to the same cloud folder sees the same library. The app decides what moves, checks every file before it enters the library, and never replaces or deletes anything to settle a conflict.
